title: Draft schema for x-bte annotation refactor
description: Manually-written schema for x-bte annotation refactor. Work-in-progress.

info.description: Required, fixed field in OpenAPI schema. Provides metadata about the API.

x-bte.description: Optional field to provide API info that the tool needs for querying or post-processing.

batch_size_limit.description: Maximum number of input IDs per request (if an annotation's request_info.support_batch: true.

request_rate_limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute from each client.

primary_key_edge_attributes.description: List of TRAPI edge-attribute keys (attribute_type_id) that distinguish unique edges. If attribute X is listed here and two constructed TRAPI edges only differ by attribute X's value, the tool should be keep both of them as separate edges.

x-bte-annotations.description: One or more x-bte annotations go here. One x-bte annotation describes a subset of data available using the API (semantics), how to query for this data, and how to process the response (assumed to be JSON). The main fields that define a unique x-bte annotation are: path (endpoint), request method, and core 'metaedge' info - input category, predicate, qualifier-set, and output category. Keys are user-defined names (allowed characters set using patternProperties) that generally note the dataset and semantic relationship.

^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$.description: This is the subschema for a single annotation. Properties are snake_case.

response_field_root.description: If every response-field's path (JSON dot-notation) has the same root, that root can be specified in this optional property. If specified, then every response-field should only specify the path from this root. Don't include a trailing '.', and don't need to specify the arrays traversed.

inputs.description: Describes the input bioentities (and their IDs). These are put in the API request to retrieve their biological relationship data.

use_all_namespaces.description: Only use when the namespaces array has >1 element. If an input entity has synonymous IDs from >1 namespace listed in the 'namespaces' section, should the tool generate queries using all of those IDs (true)? True implies that the API may have different data for the same biological thing but under IDs in different namespaces, and you want to retrieve all of that data. Or should the tool only use the IDs for 1 namespace - the first in the 'namespaces' section that it has IDs for (false)? False implies that the API has already done an 'entity-resolution' step and an ID from any namespace would retrieve the same data. If this field isn't specified, the tool defaults to 'false' behavior.
use_all_namespaces.$comment: While `outputs` also has this field, the description is different.

namespaces.description: List of possible ID namespaces for input bioentities. They should be in order of preference (see 'use_all_namespaces' property's description).
namespaces.$comment: outputs also has this property. Right now, I'm defining the two separately because the required properties are different.

id_field.description: If request_info.support_batch is true, there should be a response-field in each hit that specifies the matched input ID. The path to this field should be specified here in JSON dot-notation (don't need to specify the arrays traversed).
id_field.$comment: outputs also has this property. Right now, I'm defining them separately because the description is different.

predicate.description: This is the biomedical-science semantic type of the relationship between the input and output entities. The value must be a predicate in the biolink-model: it should be the most specific predicate that matches the relationship. Predicates labeled 'mixin' should be used carefully (read yaml spec before using). The format is snake_case, no prefix. Validation is currently just on format, so it doesn't check whether the value actually exists in the biolink-model version the tool is using.
predicate.$comment: For full validation, this would need enum of biolink-model predicates. And would need to be maintained, up-to-date with biolink-model version the tool is using.

qualifiers.description: This is 1 static set of biolink-model qualifiers that add nuance and detail to the relationship between the input and output entities. The keys should be specific qualifiers from the biolink-model, and the values should be from the biolink-model enums for those qualifiers. No prefixes are needed for keys or values.
qualifiers.$comment: Not specifying every recommended qualifier_type_id right now. TBH I'm not sure what a complete set would be. So giving the basic format. qualifier_type_id are snake_case and generally end in '_qualifier'. values are snake-case.

outputs.description: Describes the output bioentities (and their IDs). These should be in the API's response along with any data on the biological relationship between the input and output bioentities.

use_all_namespaces.description: Only use when the namespaces array has >1 element. If 1 hit in the response has output IDs from >1 namespace listed in the 'namespaces' section, should the tool ingest all those IDs (true)? True implies that the API may return multiple entities in 1 hit. Or should the tool only ingest the ID(s) from 1 namespace - the first in the 'namespaces' section that it finds IDs for (false)? False implies that either (1) 1 hit only has 1 output ID, or (2) the multiple output IDs in 1 hit represent the same entity so only 1 of the IDs is needed. If this field isn't specified, the tool defaults to 'false' behavior. It may be rare to set this field to true.

namespaces.description: List of possible ID namespaces for output bioentities. They should be in order of preference (see 'use_all_namespaces' property's description).

id_field.description: Specifies the path to the response-field that contains the output ID (assuming field's value is a single ID, using 'capture_regex' if needed). This path should be JSON dot-notation (don't need to specify the arrays traversed).

capture_regex.description: Sometimes, the response-field's string value is not the expected format and cannot be handled with replace_prefix (suffixes, ID format isn't biolink-model or bioregistry standard, delimited string, etc). This field can be used to provide a capturing group (regex) to retrieve the ID in the expected format. Exact flavor of regex TBD, assume PCRE2 for now.

exclude_namespace_combos.description: Only use this field if inputs.namespaces AND outputs.namespaces both have >1 element. If a few input/output namespaces combos don't exist in the API's data, these combos can be listed here so the tool can skip them. If this field AND include_namespace_combos are not specified, the tool will assume that the API data may include all possible combos of input and output namespace.

include_namespace_combos.description: Similar to 'exclude_namespace_combos', except this field is for listing combos that exist in the API's data. Annotation writers SHOULD NOT specify both fields in the same annotation (just specify one). There may be edge-cases where it's preferable to use this field over 'exclude...'. Ex: input/output have a LOT of namespaces but only a small amount of combos actually exist.
include_namespace_combos.$comment: if exclude_namespace_combos is used, then this one shouldn't be used and vice versa. Add logic to schema later?

request_info.description: Info needed to generate the API request
request_info.$comment: Needs complex validation logic for {request_body, parameters, by_input_namespace, by output_namespace}: at least 1 of these needs to exist. If one of the by_... exist, than no other fields can (VS request_body, parameters can be together). Within by_..., they need at least 1 of {request_body, parameters}.

path.description: Which endpoint the request should be sent to. This MUST be a relative path (from the API server url) listed in the 'paths' section of the OpenAPI/SmartAPI spec.

method.description: Which http method (ex: get vs post) the request should use. This MUST be a method specified for the 'path' endpoint in the 'paths' section of the OpenAPI/SmartAPI spec.

support_batch.description: Can multiple input IDs be sent in 1 request (true) or not (false)

content_type.description: Use this field to specify the content type (aka media type) of the request body. If not specified, the default is 'application/json'. The annotation writer is responsible for specifying a request body that matches this content type.

use_pagination.description: Is this request using API pagination (true), or not (false)? Default is false.
use_pagination.$comment: For now, note info needed for/related to pagination in notes doc. Deciding where this info goes and its format later.

by_input_namespace.description: Sometimes, different request info is needed for the different input or output namespaces. Examples: different parameter / request_body values; needing separate queries to avoid matching input IDs to the wrong namespace's data (this can happen when IDs aren't prefixed and have the same format). The keys are namespace prefixes, and the values are namespace-specific request_info. If by_input_namespace is used, then by_output_namespace SHOULD NOT be used, and vice versa.

by_output_namespace.$comment: the same structure as by_input_namespace. May put the contents in def and ref here. But would need description that works for both.

provenance.$comment: complex!!! one of 3 schemas (two object, 1 array). Have some nested parts that are kinda repetitive, can make $ref to $def.

response_mapping.description: Map response-fields to TRAPI edge properties, generally edge attributes. The keys can be chosen from a set of keywords (linked to specific ways of parsing the response-field's value and setting up the TRAPI edge property), OR the keys can be CURIEs (prefix:ID) from the biolink-model or a standard ontology that describe the edge-attribute. The values should be the JSON dot-notation path for the response field (don't need to specify the arrays traversed). Advice: users generally want references (publication IDs), publication text snippets (if text-mined), and other structured info.

^([A-Za-z]+):([A-Za-z]+)$.description: patternProperties (keys) are CURIEs (prefix:ID) from the biolink-model or a standard ontology that describe the edge-attribute.

edge-attributes.description: The response-field's value is a complete set of TRAPI edge-attributes (already in the desired format). The tool should ingest this with no changes.

trapi_sources.description: The response-field's value is a set of TRAPI edge source objects (already in the desired format). The tool should ingest this with no changes.

source_url.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more urls to the primary source's external webpages for this specific edge/relationship. It should be added to the primary-knowledge-source object, under the 'source_record_urls' property.

ref_pmid.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more PMIDs of publications that support this edge. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix PMID) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_url.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more urls for webpages that support this edge. These should be kept as-is and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_pmcid.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more PMCIDs of publications that support this edge. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix PMCID?) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_clinicaltrials.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more clinical trial NCT IDs that support this edge. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix clinicaltrials, ID should start with NCT) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_doi.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more DOI for publications that support this edge. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix doi) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_isbn.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more ISBN for publications that support this edge. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix isbn) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

test_examples.description: This section is optional but very useful for testing, so highly recommended to fill out. This is a list of input/output ID pairs that a tool should be able to retrieve from the API using this annotation. These IDs should be in CURIE format (namespace's standard prefix, colon-delimiter, ID in standard format for namespace).

if.$comment: If document has x-bte tag or components.x-bte-annotations, then the other should also be present. See x-translator, x-trapi for examples of how to write this. Don't need to write out the tags section elsewhere in schema. There's also other possible if-then statements (look up 'if' in schema).

category.description: This is the biomedical-science semantic type of the entities represented by these IDs. The value must be a class (aka node category) in the biolink-model: it should be the most specific class that fits most of the entities. Avoid using classes labeled 'mixin' when possible. The format is PascalCase, no prefix. Validation is currently just on format, so it doesn't check whether the value actually exists in the biolink-model version the tool is using.
category.$comment: For full validation, this would need enum of acceptable biolink-model node categories (not mixins and must be bioentities?). And would need to be maintained, up-to-date with biolink-model version the tool is using.

name_field.description: Optional field to specify response-field for the human-readable name/label of the ID. The tool will use this name for the entity if the ID-resolving service doesn't find a human-readable name for the entity's ID. Use JSON dot-notation to specify the path to this field (don't need to specify the arrays traversed).

parameters.description: Specifies the request parameters. These DO NOT NEED to be specified in endpoint/method's subsection within the 'paths' section of the OpenAPI/SmartAPI spec. The annotation writer has the variables {{input_ids}} (array of IDs w/o prefix) and {{input_curies}} (array of IDs with prefix) to denote where the input IDs go in the parameters (if needed). Jinja2 templating is available to transform those arrays into delimited strings or specify more complex transforms.

prefix.description: This is the standard prefix for the ID namespace. Its format should be (in order of preference): what the biolink-model uses, what [bioregistry](https://bioregistry.io/) specifies, or the prefix used by the resource that created the ID namespace. The delimiter is assumed to be ':' and should not be included.

prefix_combo.description: 2-element array: the first element is the input namespace's prefix, the second is output namespace's prefix.

replace_prefix.description: Sometimes, an API will use a non-standard ID prefix or delimiter for entities (differs from the standard specified in 'prefix' and a colon-delimiter). This non-standard ID prefix AND its delimiter should be specified here. It is important to include this when the non-standard prefix must be added to input IDs for queries or will be in the output id_field's value.

request_body.description: Specifies the request body. The annotation writer has the variables {{input_ids}} (array of IDs w/o prefix) and {{input_curies}} (array of IDs with prefix) to denote where the input IDs go in the request body. Jinja2 templating is available to transform those arrays into delimited strings or specify more complex transforms.
